{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABYkREXw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhCJIJ4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 19, "title": "Expand remaining WebXR API coverage in one consolidated implementation pass", "body": "## Problem

The emulator has modernized its core WebXR Device, Hit Test, Gamepad, Hand Input, Anchors, Depth Sensing, Lighting Estimation, and basic Layers APIs, and now provides an opt-in Interactive DOM Overlay Preview. However, the [current capability inventory](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/webxr-conformance.md) still lists several unsupported WebXR modules and partial implementations. Applications using those APIs cannot be meaningfully tested against the Quest 3 VR/MR and Generic Android Phone AR profiles.

**Use one umbrella Issue for this effort.** Do not create a separate Issue for every missing API/module. Implement as many reasonably feasible gaps as possible together, focusing on deterministic, useful *simulation* rather than physical-sensor fidelity or perfect specification conformance. Some modules may be too difficult or require browser/OS support; those must be investigated and **reported in a GitHub PR comment**, not silently ignored, stubbed as functional, or allowed to block all the practical work.

## Expected outcome

Make one coordinated pass over the missing and incomplete WebXR surface, implementing **as many realistically achievable APIs as possible** in the existing TypeScript emulator and testing the resulting behavior.

Prioritize (subject to technical feasibility and actual applicable specification maturity):

1. **Environmental geometry:** Plane Detection and Mesh Detection, using the existing deterministic virtual-room geometry and Hit Test scene where possible. Expose meaningful tracked plane/mesh data, transforms, update/lifecycle behavior, and capability negotiation instead of just empty objects.
2. **Image Tracking:** investigate an opt-in simulated image-target system (known target/pose supplied through the DevTools scene/configuration rather than pretending to access a real camera); implement the application-facing module if the relevant spec contract and a useful deterministic behavior can be supported.
3. **Reference spaces and navigation:** `bounded-floor`, `unbounded` or related missing session/space behavior where a faithful-enough virtual-world model is feasible. Do not claim tracking bounds or unbounded tracking without a usable implementation.
4. **Complete practical subsets of existing modules:** persistent Anchors (if safely simulated across sessions), additional Layers (e.g., cylinder/equirect/cube or texture formats/arrays), GPU Depth Sensing or further formats, Lighting Estimation reflections, and other clearly useful missing operations. Choose coherent implementations that match available WebGL/runtime capabilities.
5. **Other missing or platform-dependent APIs:** camera access, secondary views, WebGPU-based XR rendering, haptics, or newly relevant WebXR modules. Research applicability and feasibility; implement only where a safe, verifiable emulation is genuinely practical. Distinguish WebXR specification modules from browser/gamepad/platform extension APIs, and never fake real camera/sensor data or privileged hardware access.

Review the **current published specs/Editor's Drafts** for the chosen modules and record their pinned versions. The above is a discovery/priority inventory, **not a promise that every item can be delivered** in this PR.

## Context

- Default/integration branch: `dev`. Follow the repository [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/review-guidelines.md) and PR template, writing Issue/PR/review comments in English.
- Source of truth before starting: [WebXR API inventory and limitations](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/webxr-conformance.md), `src/devices.json`, `src/polyfill/api/`, `src/polyfill/EmulatedXRDevice.ts`, `src/polyfill/ARScene.ts`, `src/polyfill/device-adapter.ts`, `src/polyfill/webgl.ts`, `tests/conformance.ts`, `tests/browser-smoke.ts`, `tests/wpt.ts`, and `tests/samples.ts`.
- Current limitations include unsupported plane/mesh detection, camera access, GPU depth, secondary views, WebGPU and haptics; reference spaces beyond `viewer`/`local`/`local-floor`; session-only Anchors; CPU float32-only Depth; fixed virtual Lighting without reflections; and projection + mono quad Layers with many variants unsupported. Verify source behavior rather than assuming the matrix remains unchanged.
- [Issue #17](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/issues/17) delivered a deliberately limited Interactive DOM Overlay Preview. **Keep that pragmatic preview behavior**; native `:xr-overlay`, Quest stereo DOM compositor, and full UA overlay conformance are not prerequisites for this task. Do not reintroduce the security/interaction concerns documented under earlier Issues #13/#15.
- Emulation is limited to the two existing device profiles and their supported VR/MR/AR modes. No physical headset, tracking camera, sensor access, additional browser permissions, remote scripts, or experimental browser flags should be necessary to run the main extension.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] **Inventory and triage:** Verify the remaining unsupported/partial APIs against current code and relevant specifications. Create a single status matrix in the PR body and/or `docs/webxr-conformance.md` with each module, mode/profile applicability, required core methods/data, feasibility, and decision: **implemented**, **partially implemented**, **unsupported/deferred**, or **not applicable**. Do not create individual API Issues as part of this pass.
- [ ] **Implement practical gaps:** Deliver at least one meaningful newly supported API/module (not just a constructor, feature string, constant, empty result, or unconditional stub) and implement as many other reasonably achievable items as can be safely validated within this consolidated pass. Prioritize room-backed Plane/Mesh Detection and other existing-scene/reusable capabilities. Use judgment to stop investigating disproportionately expensive items and move on to feasible work.
- [ ] **Feature truthfulness:** For every newly enabled descriptor, implement observable functional behavior and appropriate object lifetime, session/frame ownership, input validation, and `NotSupportedError`/other error semantics. Required unsupported features must reject; optional unsupported features must be omitted. Preserve sensible Quest VR/MR and Android AR capability distinctions and avoid claiming physical-sensor fidelity.
- [ ] **Virtual environment coherence:** New geometry/target data should follow the simulated room/device pose and agree with Hit Test, Anchors, viewer transforms, and other implemented APIs where relevant. Avoid independently invented data that contradicts the scene. User-facing configuration/control should be added only when needed for an actually implemented emulated capability.
- [ ] **Hard/impractical APIs are explicitly allowed to remain unsupported.** Document their real blockers (e.g., unsupported WebGL pathways, spec instability, untestable semantics, privileged/native browser features, major architectural redesign, security constraints) and leave correct negative behavior; **do not enable misleading pseudo-support simply to increase the count.**
- [ ] **Mandatory GitHub PR comment for deferred items:** Before merge, post a **human-readable top-level comment on the consolidated implementation PR**, titled **"Remaining WebXR API gaps and blockers"**, listing **every investigated but not completed API/module**, whether partial or wholly unsupported, the reason it was not practical in this pass, the current rejection/omission behavior, and a concrete future direction or prerequisite where known. Also explicitly state when there are no deferred items. Keep this visible in the **PR comments**, not only a local document, commit message or PR description. If new blockers emerge during review, update with a follow-up PR comment. This is part of completion acceptance.
- [ ] **Test actual behavior:** Add meaningful unit/API conformance and real unpacked-extension browser tests for each newly enabled capability. Cover feature negotiation, returned geometry/data, pose transforms, lifecycle, errors, and interactions with existing WebXR APIs; add representative external sample tests/WPT coverage when feasible. Record results rather than merely adding expected-pass checkboxes.
- [ ] **Preserve existing functionality:** Quest VR/MR and Android AR sessions, current controller/hand, anchors, depth, lighting, projection/quad layer drawing, Hit Test, Interactive DOM Overlay Preview, Manifest V3/CSP, and extension panel interactions must continue functioning.
- [ ] Run and accurately report `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:firefox`, `npm run test:browser`, plus relevant `npm run test:wpt` and `npm run test:samples`. Separate actual passes from not-run tests and don't claim full WPT/physical-device/browser-compatibility coverage.
- [ ] Update the README and [conformance inventory](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/webxr-conformance.md) with *verified* capabilities, configuration and limitations, plus the exact features intentionally left unsupported. Ensure the API-status matrix and mandatory **PR blocker comment** agree.
- [ ] Submit **one consolidated PR targeting `dev`** for the practical implementation pass, referencing this Issue and following the PR/review template. **Completion means the feasible set was implemented and tested, every remaining candidate was assessed and documented in the PR comment, and no misleading capabilities were advertised.** It does **not** mean that every feature in the initial inventory is implemented or that the entire WebXR standard is covered. Any later improvements may be handled in a subsequent umbrella Issue if desired.

## Optional validation

- Run Firefox MV3 extension runtime tests if an appropriate environment is available; Firefox package generation alone is not runtime validation.
- Exercise public WebXR Plane Detection, Mesh Detection, Image Tracking or other relevant samples when available and applicable.
- Compare simulated scene data against richer room fixtures, different device poses, or WPT modules beyond the already-selected five files.
- Consider broader XR standards/platform integration only after the smaller, useful emulator features work.

## Required post-merge verification

None. The PR comment describing deferred features, implementation tests, API matrix, and documentation must be completed **before** merge. Store publication and physical hardware certification are outside this Issue.
